chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Miskān and Faḍālah, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Miskān, from Muḥammad al-Ḥalabī, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: A person in janabah may have only a small amount of water with him, and if he performs ghusl with it, he fears thirst. Should he perform ghusl with it, or do tayammum? He said: “Rather, he should do tayammum; and likewise if he intends wudu (ablution).”

key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: a person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْعَطَشَ: thirst feared as a result of using the water
key_terms.الْمَاءُ الْقَلِيلُ: a small amount of water insufficient to use without hardship
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمُ: performs tayammum (dry ablution) as a substitute purification

ai.seo_question: If a person in janabah has only a little water and fears thirst, should he perform ghusl or tayammum?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one in janabah who possesses only a small amount of water and fears thirst if he uses it. The Imam عليه السلام rules that tayammum should be performed instead of ghusl, and the same ruling applies when wudu (ablution) is needed.
